$schema_doc: The YouTube community posts of the AI Engineering Simplified channel (@aiEngineeringSimplified), one object per post, the same shape as yt-posts.json (the crypto channel's queue). Rows come from the ytpost lane (python video-creation/longform-edited/graph/run.py ytpost), which picks this queue when the live video is on this channel, for a longform-edited or a longform-presentation video (Mike, 2026-11-17). Slide images live in schedule-tweets/images/ai-yt/. Status flow: 'pending' (queued) -> 'posted' (posted_at and post_url set). Posted by schedule-tweets/scripts/post_yt_community.py --channel ai (Python; its own ai-ytbot-profile, CDP 9225; first post 2026-11-17). The JS post-yt-community.js posts only the crypto channel: never run it for this file. Shown on the dashboard's AI YouTube Posts tab.

posts.body:
▶ Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/U26NDilqCDo

Every keep or kill at my human gate is now an eval score

→ 98 clips judged on record, 82.7 percent precision
→ 11 of 17 kills were one half of a full clip and impact cut pair

#AIEngineering #LLMEvals #LangGraph

images.slide_text: Two kinds of harness / An agent harness runs the loop and hands the model its tools. An evaluation harness runs the evals end to end and adds up the results.
Rules live in the code / A rule that only lives in the context is a request. The prompt explains the job. The code enforces the rules.
A score moves by itself / 83.3 / Same prompt, same transcript, same model. The difference was one impact cut.
What the record shows / 82.7% / 184 lines covering 21 livestreams, every keep or kill on record.
Opinions become replays / Can a cheaper model pick as well? That used to be an opinion. Now it's a replay.
Watch the full video / Evals in Production: Turning Human Verdicts Into a Score
